To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we derived a gauge invariant electromagnetic two point function for heavy-light systems and that we showed that this two point function can be used in the QCD sum rules method.
the QCD sum rules can be applied to the electromagnetic two-point function of heavy-light systems.

the QCD sum rules method can be extended to incorporate electromagnetic effects for heavy-light quarks and that the resulting electromagnetic corrections to the mass difference of the Ds and D0 mesons are in agreement with experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a gauge invariant electromagnetic two point function.
the development of the QCD sum-rule method for the investigation of the violation of the isospin symmetry.
a gauge invariant two-point function for the electromagnetic current of heavy-light quark system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QCD sum rules for the two-point function are not only consistent with, but also extend the results of the chiral perturbation theory.
the gauge-invariant electromagnetic two-point function is the correct one for the heavy-light quark system.
the QCD sum rules are a useful and powerful tool to investigate the properties of the hadronic states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electromagnetic two-point function can be derived in a gauge invariant way, and that the electromagnetic two point function for the heavy-light quark system is obtained by taking the limit mQ -> infinity of that for the light quark.
the gauge invariance of the electromagnetic interaction can be maintained in the sum rule method.
the gauge-invariant electromagnetic two-point function is obtained by using the heavy quark effective theory (HQET), which is a consistent method to introduce QED into QCD sum rule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QCD sum rules for the electromagnetic two-point functions can be formulated in the same way as those for the hadron two-point functions.
the gauge-invariant electromagnetic two-point function is given by a gauge-invariant product of the quark and the photon currents.
the QCD sum rules can be extended to the case of the electromagnetic two-point function.
